entities.summary: The International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC) is a global institution that represents chemists in individual countries, headquartered in Zurich. Founded in 1919, IUPAC aims to promote the advancement of chemistry worldwide by standardizing nomenclature, defining chemical symbols, and regulating the use of chemical substances. IUPAC's work has significant regional and thematic impact, particularly in the fields of chemical safety, environmental protection, and the development of new materials. Through its collaborations with national chemical societies and international organizations, IUPAC plays a crucial role in shaping the global chemical landscape. IUPAC's legacy can be seen in the widespread adoption of its standardized nomenclature, which has simplified communication among chemists and facilitated scientific discovery. The organization's commitment to chemical safety has also saved countless lives and prevented environmental disasters. Today, IUPAC continues to evolve, addressing the challenges of a rapidly changing world and promoting sustainable chemical practices.
